summary: Pendleton County, WV summit: 1916 wooden fire lookout is gone. The register says it was replaced by a stone-faced concrete observation tower; the summit tower finished in 1969 may be that replacement (not stated outright). Registered as a former lookout site in 2017.

facts.design: Register: the 1916 wooden lookout 'has since been replaced with a stone-faced concrete observation tower'. Byrd Center: the 1969 summit observation tower has two levels of observation platforms and an enclosed space for exhibit panels. NPS: a two-story observation tower stands at the peak. The register does not date the replacement or name the 1969 tower.
facts.status_note: The 1916 wooden fire lookout is gone. A visitor observation tower stands on the summit, finished 1969. Register and Forest Fire Lookout Association lists do not describe the observation tower as a lookout.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Monongahela National Forest

access.note: The observation tower is found along the half-mile Whispering Spruce Trail that circles the mountain top (National Park Service). No closure found in the sources read; current conditions not checked.

visit.trail_note: Half-mile Whispering Spruce Trail circles the summit and passes the observation tower (National Park Service).

events.note: Lookout station under construction on the summit at 4,860 ft, per the 4th Biennial Report of the state Forest, Game and Fish Warden.
Moses R. Bennett put on duty as watchman in spring 1916, before the station was finished, to meet local people and distribute literature.
Summit observation tower finished in summer 1969 after work in 1966 and 1967; dedicated 13 September 1969 with a keynote by Senator Robert Byrd.
Registered 26 January 2017 as US 1641, WV 32, nominated by Brian Powell.

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association West Virginia list marks the entry Gone, not standing. The register says the wooden tower was replaced. The standing structure is the later observation tower, which is not the lookout record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief said the lookout listing was standing and the register was gone. The current FFLA list reads Gone and the register says the wooden tower was replaced. The fire lookout is gone; the visitor observation tower stands.

notes_for_editor: Date the wooden lookout came down is not found, so no removal event is recorded. Whether the 1969 observation tower replaced it is inferred from the register wording and not stated outright in any fetched source. The brief's elevation (1482.2 m) is the summit height, not a tower height; no height key is given. Brief status corrected: the FFLA list reads Gone. Two WebSearch results (a Monongahela guide saying the stone tower stands on a former wooden tower site, and a 1938 photo of a fire tower) were not fetched, so they are not used. The FFLA list's Gone status and the register's wording fit together, so the record is not contradictory once the observation tower is separated from the fire lookout. Used 2 WebSearch calls and 6 page reads.
